titulo: Experiment: keep or discard based on a single metric
lead: The cleanest design for a loop that improves on its own is short: the agent changes one thing, a command gives the score, if it improved it stays with a commit, if it didn't it goes back with git reset, and everything becomes one line in a file. In this lesson you run this cycle with fake agents and then with the real Claude Code.
objetivo: run an autoresearch-style experiment: the agent changes, a single metric decides, git commit if it improved and git reset if not.

aprende.t: Keep = commit, discard = reset: git as undo
A single metric, with a fixed budget per cycle
results.tsv: every attempt becomes a line, including the bad ones
The same cycle with a fake agent and with Claude Code

hero_alt: Two circuit boards side by side connected to meters; one with a yellow tag, the other going into the discard bin.

secoes.sub: The autoresearch design, as described in secondary sources. Click each block.

nos.detalhe: The cycle starts by measuring the system as it is (in the rehearsal, 0.700 = 28 of 40 cases). The repo must be clean: a loose change before the cycle mixes two experiments.
The agent changes the system (here, regras.txt). One change per cycle: with two, you don't know which one moved the score.
The same command as the baseline, on the same set of cases. A single metric decides; the others, if any, are "do not worsen" (lessons 3 and 6).
It improved: commit with the score in the message. The next attempt starts from here.
Equal or worse: git reset --hard and git clean. Nothing is left half-done. The bad attempt stays recorded in results.tsv, so nobody tests it again.

secoes.volta: next cycle starts from the last keep
secoes.legenda: In autoresearch the system is a training script and the metric is validation loss; here, a triage classifier with 40 synthetic cases.
secoes.dica: Equal is not better: a tie goes to discard. Otherwise the system piles up changes that do nothing.

secoes.sub: Four ideas, one per cycle. One of them breaks on the first run (the agent is left without an answer). Run it, interrupt it, and resume.

msg.inicio: Four ideas waiting. Click "Run the cycles".
msg.rodando: One cycle at a time: base → agent → measure → keep or discard.
msg.parou: Interrupted midway: the change was left loose in the repo. experimento.sh refuses to start with a dirty repo until you undo it with git reset --hard.
msg.retoma: Resumed from scratch: the interrupted idea runs all over again, starting from the last keep.
msg.fim: Queue empty: each idea became a line in results.tsv.
msg.fimfalha: Queue empty. One idea ended in error (agent gave no answer): that is an error, never "did not improve".

secoes.legenda: Browser simulation. The real rehearsal is right below.

secoes.sub: The kit creates a triage repo (v1) and runs three cycles: an agent that improves, one that makes things worse, and one that does not change the score. No model is called.

Treating an agent with no answer as "did not improve". When your subscription hits its limit, the agent returns empty: the cycle must come out as an error (code 2), otherwise the queue turns into a series of false discards and nobody notices that nothing ran. agente-claude.sh exits with 1 when the answer has no rules, and experimento.sh records erro.

secoes.titulo: The same cycle with Claude Code
secoes.sub: One call through your subscription (uses your subscription quota): claude -p with no tools receives the rules and the wrong cases and returns a new regras.txt. The measurement decides, not the model.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-aprende-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-aprende/a2      # the rehearsal repo above, already with the synonyms keep
AGENTE="bash $K/agente-claude.sh" bash $K/experimento.sh $E/sis "claude: uma mudança"; echo "saída: $?"
echo "status da última linha: $(tail -1 $E/sis/results.tsv | cut -f5)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# agente-claude.sh — o agente REAL do experimento: o Claude Code (sem ferramentas) propõe um regras.txt novo.
# Roda na pasta do repo, chamado pelo experimento.sh. Sai da cota da sua assinatura (uma chamada).
# Resposta vazia (limite da sessão, erro) = ERRO, saída 1: nunca vira "não mudou nada".
set -uo pipefail
K=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
PEDIDO="Você melhora as regras de um classificador de mensagens de suporte. Formato de cada linha: 'categoria: palavra, palavra'; a primeira categoria cuja palavra aparece no texto vence; sem nenhuma, 'outros'.
Regras atuais:
$(cat regras.txt)

Casos que o classificador errou:
$(python3 "$K/medir.py" . --erros | tail -n +2)

Proponha UMA mudança que generalize (palavras que pessoas reais usariam), sem copiar frases inteiras dos casos.
Responda SÓ com o conteúdo completo do novo regras.txt, sem explicação e sem cercas de código."
J=$(mktemp)
echo "$PEDIDO" | claude -p --tools "" --output-format json > "$J" 2>/dev/null
python3 - "$J" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys
try:
    d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
except Exception:
    print("ERRO: resposta do claude não é JSON"); sys.exit(1)
r = (d.get("result") or "").strip()
linhas = [l for l in r.splitlines() if not l.startswith("```")]
if d.get("is_error") or not any(":" in l for l in linhas):
    print("ERRO: sem regras na resposta (" + (r[:80] or "vazia") + ")"); sys.exit(1)
u = d.get("usage") or {}
ent = u.get("input_tokens", 0) + u.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) + u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0)
if os.environ.get("TOKENS_ARQ"):
    open(os.environ["TOKENS_ARQ"], "w").write(f"{ent} {u.get('output_tokens', 0)}\n")
open("regras.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(linhas).strip() + "\n")
print(f"regras.txt reescrito ({len(linhas)} linhas)")
PY
rc=$?; rm -f "$J"; exit $rc

exercicios.texto: In your system, write the command that prints the metric of your hypothesis (lesson 1) as a number on one line, in the format of medir.py --valor. Replace the medir.py in experimento.sh with yours (or adapt your system to the rules + cases format).

perguntas.p: The change gave exactly the same score as the base. What does the cycle do?
opcoes: Keep, because it did not get worse
Discard: a tie is not an improvement
Run again until the score changes
perguntas.explica: A tie resulting in keep piles up changes that do nothing and make the system harder to read. experimento.sh requires the new score to be greater than the base.

perguntas.p: Why does the discard also go into results.tsv?
opcoes: So the bad idea is not tested again and to measure the loop's hit rate
It doesn't: only the keep is recorded; the discard disappears along with the git reset, leaving no trace at all
perguntas.explica: The record of bad attempts is the loop's memory, just like memoria/descartados.md in LOOP-R. And lesson 7 takes the cost per keep from it.

perguntas.p: The agent gave no answer (session limit). How should the cycle end?
opcoes: Silence: try on the next one
perguntas.explica: A missing answer is an error, never "did not improve". Otherwise the queue produces false discards and nobody sees that nothing ran.

perguntas.p: About the autoresearch numbers (experiments per hour, training gain), what does this course say?
opcoes: They come from the official peer-reviewed paper, with published code and data
They are reported by secondary sources, with no confirmation
perguntas.explica: The track's research only found the design and the numbers in secondary sources. The design (single metric, fixed budget, git as undo) is what you take from it.

itens.texto: Each cycle measures the baseline, lets the agent change one thing, and measures again with the same command.
Improved is a commit; equal or worse is a reset. Nothing is left half done.
results.tsv stores keep, discard and erro; an empty answer from the model is an error.
